children: Sibanye-Stillwater could cut around 1,000 roles at its Rustenburg mine in South Africa as it closes the Kwezi shaft.

The platinum group metals miner said it would consult with employees as the shaft comes to the end of its economic life. The shaft had been expected to close as it reaches the limits of the area it is licensed to mine.
Efforts to keep the shaft operational faced stakeholder objections and permit delays, the company said.
The shaft produced less than 3% of the group's South African PGM production in the first half of the year and booked losses in 2024 and 2025.
Around 781 employees and 333 contractor employees could be affected but no final decision had been made, the company said.
Sibanye-Stillwater has a global workforce of more than 70,000, according to its website.
